headline: Acquisitions drive revenue up, but EPS swings to a loss
summary_short: Shift4 reported Q1 2026 gross revenue of $1,121M (+32.2% y/y), driven by acquisitions and 24% higher payment volume, but net income attributable to the company fell 11.8% y/y to $15M and diluted EPS swung to a $(0.01) loss after $16M of newly accrued preferred dividends and higher acquisition-debt interest expense.
summary_long: Gross revenue rose 32.2% y/y to $1,121M on 24% higher payment volume, recent acquisitions, and the first quarter of TFS revenue from Global Blue ($102M). Income from operations doubled y/y to $50M, but GAAP net income fell 11.8% y/y to $15M and diluted EPS swung to $(0.01) from $0.20, mainly on $16M of newly accrued Series A preferred dividends and a $36M y/y rise in interest expense tied to 2025 acquisition debt. Company-reported Adjusted EBITDA rose 39% y/y to $234M. Cash fell to $473M from $964M q/q as $295M of share buybacks, $139M of Simplification Transaction cash paid to Rook, and $15M of preferred dividends outweighed $134M of operating cash flow. No forward guidance was included in this 10-Q.

drivers.explanation: The filing leads with gross revenue up 32%, or $273M, driven by a 24% rise in processing volume, recent acquisitions, and the first-ever quarter of TFS revenue from Global Blue.
Payments-based revenue grew 21% on a 24% rise in processing volume plus recent acquisitions; the $102M of TFS revenue is entirely new following the Q3 2025 Global Blue acquisition.

Swing to a diluted loss per share reflects $16M of newly accrued Series A preferred dividends and a $36M y/y rise in interest expense from 2025 Global Blue acquisition debt, outweighing the operating-income gain.

Net income fell y/y even as operating income roughly doubled, because a $36M rise in interest expense and a swing to a pretax loss offset a larger income tax benefit; not framed as a single driver in the filing.
Company states G&A and D&A increases were primarily due to recent acquisitions and business growth, while payments-based and TFS revenue growth outpaced those cost increases.

Shard figure ($392M) is a broader measure than the company's own non-GAAP gross profit ($370M); both moved with the same 32% revenue growth from acquisitions and volume, not a distinct disclosed cause.

Shard EBITDA ($188M) differs from the company's own reported EBITDA ($183M) and Adjusted EBITDA ($234M, +39% y/y per the filing); the increase tracks the same revenue growth and acquisition contribution cited for Adjusted EBITDA.

Not framed as a single driver; per the cash-flow statement, $295M of buybacks, $139M paid to Rook under the Simplification Transactions, and $15M of preferred dividends exceeded $134M of operating cash flow.

Not discussed in the filing; per the debt note, total debt principal was roughly flat q/q ($4,563M vs $4,589M) with no new issuance or repayment, so the small decline reflects FX translation on the Euro-denominated 2033 notes.

Per the equity statement, the Simplification Transactions (Up-C Collapse) added $301M of equity via the TRA waiver and preferred issuance to Rook, plus $12M of net income, partly offset by $297M of buybacks.
